H-A: ESIM solenoid (commanded vent) circuit or ECM driver never closes the vent.

CLAIM: the ESIM solenoid (the commanded vent), its circuit, or the ECM driver that energises it never closes the vent, so no vacuum can build when the ECM seals the system for its EVAP tests. Every test then fails on a system that is physically sealed. The ESIM is taken to hold two things: a switch that reports vacuum to the ECM, and a solenoid that the ECM energises to seal the vent for the tests. That split comes from the repo's test catalogue (mes.mechanic_tests describes an ESIM / EVAP vent solenoid and a separate switch parameter); no FCA description of this car's EVAP system has been obtained, so the exact split of roles on this car is unknown. If the solenoid or its driver never works, the ECM waits for a vacuum that cannot arrive, and the same failure appears after a refuel, during a cold soak and while driving. The existing hypothesis ce6bd236 covers the input side (the switch signal reaching the ECM); this one covers the output side (the command leaving the ECM and acting on the vent).

EVIDENCE FOR: (1) Three regimes, one outcome. The freeze frames read on 2026-10-19 (store dtc_detail 00:25:35 to 00:25:38; scaling medium confidence) show P0455 at idle (764 rpm, 0 km/h) at 91.8 % fuel just after a refuel, P0456 with the engine off (0 rpm, 12.3 V, MAP 969 mbar) at coolant 17 C after a cold soak, and P0440 while driving in 3rd gear (12.1 km/h, coolant 51 C). The values are evidence; that one cause fits all three is an inference. (2) The system is sealed and two ESIM units have not changed the result. Three smoke tests were clean (2025-08, 2026-09-16, 2026-09-26; job actions d5013d32, 195f9b05, 8aab8340), and the codes came both with the original ESIM (2025-09-24 to 2026-09-02) and with the new ESIM 04861961AD fitted 2026-09-02 (P0440 back by 2026-09-04). All of that is evidence. A fault that follows the car across two ESIM units points at what the unit plugs into (connector, wiring, ECM driver) rather than at the unit; that is an inference, and the new unit's fitment was never VIN-verified (unknown). (3) The one direct test of the command has never been run. The repo's MES function catalogue (mes.mes_functions, confidence CORROBORATED, from a MES support-forum thread plus the repo's own research) lists an 'ESIM commanded vent test' under Engine, ECM, Actuators. Whether this car's MES shows it on the ECM Actuators tab has not been observed (unknown; the MES install keeps its actuator list encrypted). CLAIM: the meaning of P0440 on this ECM is not established, and it may be a control-circuit style code rather than a leak-style code. MES names P0440-00 'Evaporation control valve' while it names P0455-00 and P0456-00 'Evaporation system leak' (evidence: SCAN_2610190039.txt lines 10 to 12 and 85 to 87). The repo has no verified FCA definition of P0440: mes/dtc_descriptions.py has no entry for it, and the repo's own EVAP notes describe it only as a general EVAP system fault (evidence). The generic SAE title of P0440 is an evaporative emission control system malfunction (general knowledge, not from the repo and not verified for FCA); the FCA wording and the monitor behind it are unknown. If P0440 is the ECM's ESIM control-circuit or vent-control code, the picture changes: the car's recurring P0440 would then be a direct pointer to the solenoid or driver path, and hypothesis H-A would become the lead.

EVIDENCE FOR: (1) The MES label is circuit-style ('control valve'), unlike the two leak codes (evidence). (2) P0440 is the only EVAP code that requests the lamp: status 0xCD (bit 0x80 set) on 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-19, while P0455 and P0456 read 0x4D (evidence). The repo notes that why the ECM ties the lamp to P0440 alone is not determinable from the logs (evidence); a different monitor or a different severity rule behind P0440 would be one way to explain it (inference). (3) The MES actuator that has been run 18 times on this car is also called 'Evaporation control valve' (the purge valve; the engine-side purge valve 68337662AC was replaced between 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-25), so the same label appears on a part that has been replaced and tested (evidence). CONFIRM: obtain the FCA definition of P0440 for the 2018 Stelvio 2.0T from a dealer, the wiring-diagram/workshop-manual DTC table or a bulletin text, and record it on this job with its source and date. If the definition describes the ESIM, vent solenoid or valve control circuit or driver, this hypothesis is confirmed and H-A becomes the lead. REFUTE: if the definition describes a general EVAP system or leak/vacuum monitor failure with no circuit or driver meaning, this hypothesis is refuted and nothing moves toward H-A on this ground. CLAIM: the ESIM solenoid (the commanded vent), its circuit, or the ECM driver that energises it never closes the vent, so no vacuum can build when the ECM seals the system for its EVAP tests. Every test then fails on a system that is physically sealed. The ESIM is taken to hold two things: a switch that reports vacuum to the ECM, and a solenoid that the ECM energises to seal the vent for the tests. That split comes from the repo's test catalogue (mes.mechanic_tests describes an ESIM / EVAP vent solenoid and a separate switch parameter); no FCA description of this car's EVAP system has been obtained, so the exact split of roles on this car is unknown. If the solenoid or its driver never works, the ECM waits for a vacuum that cannot arrive, and the same failure appears after a refuel, during a cold soak and while driving. The existing hypothesis ce6bd236 covers the input side (the switch signal reaching the ECM); this one covers the output side (the command leaving the ECM and acting on the vent).

EVIDENCE FOR: (1) Three regimes, one outcome. The freeze frames read on 2026-10-19 (store dtc_detail 00:25:35 to 00:25:38; scaling medium confidence) show P0455 at idle (764 rpm, 0 km/h) at 91.8 % fuel just after a refuel, P0456 with the engine off (0 rpm, 12.3 V, MAP 969 mbar) at coolant 17 C after a cold soak, and P0440 while driving in 3rd gear (12.1 km/h, coolant 51 C). The values are evidence; that one cause fits all three is an inference. (2) The system is sealed and two ESIM units have not changed the result. Three smoke tests were clean (2025-08, 2026-09-16, 2026-09-26; job actions d5013d32, 195f9b05, 8aab8340), and the codes came both with the original ESIM (2025-09-24 to 2026-09-02) and with the new ESIM 04861961AD fitted 2026-09-02 (P0440 back by 2026-09-04). All of that is evidence. A fault that follows the car across two ESIM units points at what the unit plugs into (connector, wiring, ECM driver) rather than at the unit; that is an inference, and the new unit's fitment was never VIN-verified (unknown). (3) The one direct test of the command has never been run. The repo's MES function catalogue (mes.mes_functions, confidence CORROBORATED, from a MES support-forum thread plus the repo's own research) lists an 'ESIM commanded vent test' under Engine, ECM, Actuators. Whether this car's MES shows it on the ECM Actuators tab has not been observed (unknown; the MES install keeps its actuator list encrypted). No record of it exists: the only EVAP actuator in this car's MES FES logs is 'Evaporation control valve' (the purge valve), COMPLETED x18, and the two actuator_test records in the observation store are synthetic fixtures (GapTest, FailTest, stream 'fake'). That is evidence.

EVIDENCE AGAINST: none attached to the job. Caveats on record: no ESIM or vent circuit code has set (P2422 vent, P0457, P0451, P0441, P0461 and P1CEA all read 0x40, no failure recorded, in the 2026-10-19 reads), which is evidence; whether the ECM monitors this solenoid driver at all is unknown, so the absence of a circuit code does not rule the hypothesis out. The Mode 06 purge-flow test passed on 2026-10-13 (168, within 57 to 328), which is evidence that the purge side works; it says nothing about the vent side (inference).

CONFIRM: run the MES 'ESIM commanded vent test' (ECM, Actuators tab; the repo's procedure is engine running with purge active, fuel level 15 to 85 %, only one scan tool on the OBD port) with the ESIM solenoid back-probed (meter or current clamp at the ESIM connector, driver-side rear wheel liner per the repo's case notes; fuel vapour, no sparks). No click and no current when the command is sent means the solenoid, its wiring or the ECM driver is at fault, and the fault is then located by continuity from the ESIM connector to the ECM pin and by a known-good ESIM on the same connector. REFUTE: a click with normal current shows the command path works, and the hypothesis is refuted. Note the command writes a live command to the car, so it is run by the mechanic in MES, not through CUORE's job API.

Rationale: the ESIM seals the vent with gravity-seated weighted valves (Chrysler service literature, not a reading from this car). Mounted inverted or tilted, the weights cannot seat, the vent stays open, no vacuum builds, the switch never closes, and the ECM fails P0455/P0456/P0440 in every regime, surviving an ESIM replacement fitted the same way. That fits every reading but no reading shows the mounting. Test: compare the fitted ESIM's position with the service-manual installation drawing for this VIN; if wrong, refit upright, run one full EVAP monitor without clearing, read the three status bytes. Shaking/rattle is not a valid test. Readings-only certainty table: leak-detection chain 95 %; ESIM 35 %, sealed-side leak 25 %, ESIM wiring 20 %, ECM 15 %, other 5 %; no component is proven by readings to need replacement.

2026-10-19 ESIM orientation research (outside literature, not a reading from this car): FCA ESIM = housing, vacuum contact switch, diaphragm, small weighted vacuum valve (opens ~2.2 inH2O vacuum), large weighted pressure valve (opens ~0.5 inH2O); switch closes ~1 inH2O, ~0.5-2 ohm closed (vehicleservicepros 53084355). Both weights gravity-held, so the unit must be upright. ALLDATA tech tip (2007 Ram): the ESIM can be installed in four positions, only one correct (connector at 3 o-clock on that Ram); a wrongly installed replacement brought back P0440/P0441/P0456 with the switch never showing closed. Not confirmed for the Stelvio. Bench test window: hold vacuum between 1 and 2 inH2O; above ~2.2 the vacuum valve opens by design and mimics a leak. White cylinder visible in the owner-held ESIM: probably the large weighted pressure valve (unverified).

2026-10-19 ESIM source check (outside literature, not readings). SOURCED: gravity dependent, mounted vertically, adaptor where the canister is angled (B&W tech tip bw10235esim, vehicleservicepros 53084355); ALLDATA Ram tip: four install positions, one correct, wrong one gave P0440/P0441/P0456 with switch voltage never going to 0 under vacuum, fixed by reorienting; no solenoid, ECM supplies a 5 V reference + ground, switch closing pulls the signal to 0 V (B&W/SMP); thresholds large valve ~0.5 inH2O pressure, small valve ~2.2 inH2O vacuum, switch ~1 inH2O vacuum, ~0.5-2 ohm closed (VSP). NOT FOUND: identity of the white cylinder, rattle as a valid test, any mouth-blow bench procedure (directions inferred). On-car wiring check: back-probe ESIM signal ~5 V at rest, ~0 V when vacuum closes the switch.

EVIDENCE FOR (readings): U1713-2F on 10 MES scans: 2026-06-07 09:54, 08-27, 09-02, 09-04, 09-15, 09-25 (19:56 and 20:27), 09-28, 10-14 08:59, 10-19 00:39; CUORE UDS status 0x0F (failing this cycle, not lamp-requesting) at 10-13 20:24 and 10-19 00:23 and 00:30, and absent at 09-29, 10-04, 10-08 and in CUORE's 10-14 19:02 read. Bursts: SCAN_2608271131 (first read after 81 days) listed 14 codes in 5 modules; CUORE 2026-10-13 20:24 (first live read) listed BCM U1765-86, U1736-87, U1713-2F, B1176-97, B10AA-4A, IPC U1736-86/-87, RFHUB B1040-64, all history (0x08/0x0C) except U1713. MES 10-14 08:59 added RFHUB U2054-87. ABS freeze frame of U1700-87 (FESLog_2609042001): 10.6 V at startups 14280, the same start count at which the ECM stored its 08-27 P0455 (14281; start counters look shared across modules: ABS 14359 and ECM 14357 the same evening). DTCM U0100-87 on 7 scans 08-27 to 10-19; the repo's drivetrain tables call it a whole-vehicle-sweep bystander.
First-ever codes whose first-seen window overlaps the 2026-10-14 23:58 to 00:00 wrong-bitrate listen incident (modules cleared 10-14 08:59, next read 10-19 00:39): DASM U1702-87, DTCM U0422-86: probable TOOL ARTEFACT. Seen in the 2026-09-04 and 2026-10-13 ignition-cycling sessions: possible bystanders (see doc).
OUTSIDE LITERATURE: a Stelvio owner thread (stelvioforum.com 24275, link-verified 2026-10-07 in mes/experience.py) traced a C1408-86 / C141C-86 / U0102 cascade to a low 12 V battery.

EVIDENCE AGAINST (readings): CUORE read BCM, IPC and RFHUB with no codes on 2026-10-14 19:02, 10 h and 9 km after the 08:59 clear, with the tool connected, so a connected session did not by itself store these that day. U1711/U1712 stopped after 09-25 (absent in every later BCM read) while U1713 continued, which a uniform supply fault would not do. U1765, U1736, B10AA and B1040 were absent after the 10-14 clear through 10-19. No rest, cranking or charging voltage measurement exists in any record (only 12.1 V engine-off and 10.6 V in two ABS freeze frames, 12.3 V in an ECM freeze frame, 14.4 to 14.5 V port voltage running on 10-19). No driver-reported network symptom is on record.

CONFIRM / REFUTE: confirm (a) if rest voltage is low (about 12.4 V or less after the car has sat 12 h; general automotive rule of thumb, not a Stelvio spec), cranking dips below about 9.6 V, charging is outside about 13.8 to 14.8 V, or a connector/ground shows corrosion or moisture; confirm (b) if a read taken after at least 3 tool-free days with the engine running lists nothing while a read with ignition cycling or a cable swap lists the same codes. Refute 'one condition' if separate modules show codes on separate dates with no shared session.

READINGS SYNTHESIS (2026-10-20 review, docs/research/NETWORK_PATTERN_READINGS_2026-10-20.md): the BCM is the only module with complaints in both directions (it reports the ABS and ECM as erratic; the ABS, DTCM, RFHUB and IPC report the BCM). ABS U1700-87 'BCM missing' was stored at 10.6 V (startups 14280, 2026-09-04), the only low-voltage reading on record. U1711 and U1712 always appear together (6 of 6) and the last was 2026-09-25 20:27; U1713-2F continues, failing at 14.4 V on 2026-10-19 (status 0x0F), so a uniform supply fault is not shown. Return time after a BCM clear is 2.6 to over 8.9 days. Sender versus receiver cannot be split because complaints run in both directions.

OUTSIDE LITERATURE (not readings of this car; ranking is inference): 1) unstable BCM supply or ground (fuse F82, stand-alone BCM fuse, battery, IBS) - STAR S1808000005; 2) connector/terminal fault - STAR S1708000262; 3) water in the BCM/A-pillar connector - recall 18V205 / Transport Canada 2018151 (VIN scope not known); 4) configuration mismatch after flashes; 5) CAN physical layer; 6) SGW; 7) aftermarket device on the port; 8) camera obstruction (C141B-97 only). See docs/research/NETWORK_PATTERN_LITERATURE_2026-10-20.md.

PRIORITY 2. CLAIM: the DASM (radar/driver-assist module) codes C1408-86, C141C-86, C1403-86, C1431-86, and U1701-86/U1702-87, plus the chassis-sweep codes EPS U1960-83, AFLS U0428-86 and HALF U0418-86, are receiver-side reports ('signal invalid' or 'missing message') about ESP/ABS and steering signals on the chassis CAN, not faults in the DASM, HALF, camera, ESP or EPS themselves. C141B-97 'Camera blinded/obstructed/blocked' is a separate item about what the camera can see (windshield area).

EVIDENCE FOR (readings): DASM was read on 18 MES scans. C141C-86: 06-07 09:54, 08-27, 09-04, 09-15, 09-25 (x2), 10-19. C141B-97: 09-02, 09-04, 09-25 (x2), 09-28, 10-08, 10-14, 10-19 (absent 09-15, 09-29, 10-04). C1408-86: 08-27, 09-04, 10-19. C1403-86 and C1431-86: 08-27 only. U1701-86: 06-07 10:03 only (absent at 09:54 the same morning, after a clear, during MES sessions on other modules). U1702-87: 10-19 00:39 only. DASM clear on 2026-09-04 19:53 FAILED (C1408-86, C141C-86 uncleared). Chassis sweep SCAN_2609042008 (20:08): EPS U1960-83, AFLS U0428-86, HALF U0418-86 stored; ORC, PAM, ABS clean. DASM/HALF text names signals from the ESP, EPS, ABS and steering angle sensor. U1702-87 first seen in the window overlapping the 2026-10-14 23:58 to 00:00 listen incident: probable TOOL ARTEFACT.
OUTSIDE LITERATURE: FCA bulletin 08-045-20 (April 2020, opened 2026-10-20) lists C141C-86 'Video Camera Private Can Communication Failure' with B1006-49 and C1999-86 for 2020 Giulia/Stelvio built on or before 2019-12-20, fixed by BCM Restore Vehicle Configuration plus Proxi Configuration Alignment. Model year 2020, not this 2018 car; context only. A Stelvio owner thread (stelvioforum.com 24275) traced C1408-86 + C141C-86 to a low 12 V battery.

EVIDENCE AGAINST (readings): the DASM was never read by CUORE, so there is no status byte (active, pending, confirmed) for any of these codes and no freeze frame. No driver symptom is on record: no forward-collision or driver-assist message, no lane or radar complaint. All reads had a scan tool on the port. C141B-97 is the most persistent (8 reads) and has no network explanation in its text. A web search on 2026-10-20 found no document naming C141B or C1408.

CONFIRM / REFUTE: C141B: confirm a camera-view cause if the code is absent after the glass in front of the camera is cleaned and a daylight drive, or if there is a film, sticker, crack, dashcam mount or replaced windshield in that area; refute if it persists on a clean glass. Network codes: refute as separate faults if they follow the network hypothesis (absent on a quiet read); confirm a real DASM/ESP/EPS issue only if a code is active (status 0x0F) on a quiet read or the instrument cluster shows a driver-assist message.

PRIORITY 3 (watch, no action). CLAIM: RFHUB B1040-64 'Communication with Body Computer (BCM/NBC) - plausibility' and U2054-87 are receiver-side bystanders stored when the BCM is disturbed (ignition cycling, diagnostic sessions on other modules), not a fault in the RF hub or the key system.

EVIDENCE FOR (readings): B1040-64 on 6 of 18 RFHUB reads: 2026-06-07 10:03 (absent at 09:54 the same morning, nine minutes after a clear, during MES sessions on other modules), 08-27, 09-25 20:27 (absent at 19:56; ignition cycling and live-link sessions in between), 09-28, 10-08, 10-14 08:59; CUORE 0x08 (confirmed, not failing now) on 10-13 20:24. U2054-87: 08-27 and 10-14 08:59. After the 08-27 clear it was absent on 09-02, 09-04, 09-15 and 09-25 19:56 (29 days) and appeared at 20:27 that evening. Absent on CUORE 10-14 19:02 and on CUORE plus MES 10-19.

EVIDENCE AGAINST (readings): it returns after most clears, which also fits a real intermittent BCM-to-RFHUB link; no status byte exists for a tool-free quiet read; no key, start or keyless-entry symptom is recorded either way (absence of a record, not a negative test). OUTSIDE LITERATURE: no document naming B1040 or U2054 for this car was found on 2026-10-20; an Alfa forum thread only notes that the RFHUB and BCM cross-check ignition run/start status.

CONFIRM / REFUTE: confirm a real RFHUB/BCM link problem only if B1040-64 is active (status 0x0F) on a quiet read or a key/start symptom appears; refute if it stays absent on later quiet reads.

PRIORITY 4 (comfort). CLAIM: BCM B1176-97 'Rear left window riser - component or system operation obstructed or blocked' is a local fault at the rear-left window (seal or glass-run friction, regulator, or an anti-pinch/learn state), independent of the network codes.

EVIDENCE FOR (readings): B1176-97 was FIRST SEEN 2026-08-27 11:31 (absent in both 2026-06-07 BCM scans, so not chronic since 06-07). BCM scans listing B1176-97: 2026-08-27, 09-02, 09-04, 09-15, 09-25 (19:56 and 20:27), 09-28, 09-29, 10-14 08:59 (9 scans) and CUORE status 0x08 (confirmed, not failing now) on 2026-10-13 20:24. It returned after each BCM clear from 08-27 to 09-29 (after 6, 11, 10, 3, 1 and 14 days).

EVIDENCE AGAINST (readings): it was absent on 2026-10-04 and 10-08 (5 and 9 days after the 09-29 clear) and absent again on 10-14 19:02 and 10-19 (5 days after the 10-14 clear), so it is not constant; no window symptom (slow, stopping, reversing, noise) is recorded; it has no freeze frame. A web search on 2026-10-20 found no document naming B1176 for this car (the repo's own text is a generic body-module definition).

CONFIRM / REFUTE: confirm if the rear-left window runs slowly, stops, reverses on the way up, or the glass run/seal shows friction or debris; refute if the window moves smoothly full travel both ways on several cycles and the code stays absent on later reads.

WINDOW INITIALISATION (third-party text, check the owner's handbook; anti-pinch is off during it, keep hands clear): start the car, close doors and windows; hold the switch down until fully open and a few seconds more; pull and hold up until fully closed and a few seconds more; repeat if one-touch still fails. Re-read the BCM without clearing; proof = absent longer than 14 d 9 h with the window used daily.

OWNER-ATTESTED, reported 2026-10-22 (exact repair date not given; dated to the report). ESIM replaced with a NEW unit, fitted with a NEW ESIM gasket. The previous ESIM (fitted 2026-09-02) had been installed with the ORIGINAL (reused) gasket. Meaning: a reused gasket is a possible leak path on the sealed side at the ESIM port, and is removed by this repair. Part number of the new ESIM not recorded; add it when known.

OWNER-ATTESTED, reported 2026-10-22: the previous ESIM was mounted with the WHITE CYLINDER DOWN; the new ESIM is mounted with the WHITE CYLINDER UP. Meaning: the earlier mounting was inverted relative to the new one. Outside literature (Chrysler ESIM article; B&W tip; ALLDATA Ram tip): the ESIM's weighted valves are gravity-held, it must be mounted upright, and a wrongly oriented ESIM produced P0440/P0441/P0456 with the switch never closing. Which way up is correct for this part is not stated by any source found; the identity of the white cylinder is unverified. The out-of-car blow test (handbook/esim PDF) or the completed EVAP monitor is what proves the new orientation.

next_test: REPAIR APPLIED 2026-10-22 (owner-attested): new ESIM, new gasket, white cylinder now UP (was DOWN). Proof of fix, readings only, NO CLEARING: 1) connect CUORE on the plain port and read the ECM status bytes of P0440/P0455/P0456 as the baseline (whatever MES left); 2) drive normal cycles until the EVAP monitor reports complete (cold start, fuel 1/4-3/4, steady cruise, engine-off soak); 3) read readiness, Mode 06 EVAP MIDs 0x3A/0x3C (0.090 in test TID 0x87 must be >= 3965 ms; 0.020 in test TID 0x90 within its limit) and the three status bytes; FIXED = monitor complete, Mode 06 within limits, no testFailed bits on P0440/P0455/P0456. If the codes return: run the out-of-car blow test on the removed and the new ESIM in both orientations, then back-probe the ESIM signal (5 V rest / ~0 V at ~1 inH2O vacuum).
